flat.name: Arizona
flat.note: 2.5% after the $8,350 / $16,700 standard deduction in the 2026 Tax Foundation table (static conformity to the pre-TCJA federal amount until the state adopts a later Internal Revenue Code date).

flat.name: Colorado
flat.note: 4.4% after the federal standard deduction Colorado uses for 2026.

flat.name: Georgia
flat.note: 5.19% after the standard deduction. $4,000 exemption per dependent.

flat.name: Idaho
flat.note: 5.3% after the standard deduction, on income above the zero-rate band.

flat.name: Illinois
flat.note: 4.95% after the personal exemption. No standard deduction.

flat.name: Indiana
flat.note: 2.95% after the personal exemption. County tax is not included; enter it as a local rate if you want it in the estimate.

flat.name: Iowa
flat.note: 3.8% after the federal standard deduction, minus the personal exemption credit.

flat.name: Michigan
flat.note: 4.25% after the personal exemption. City income tax is not included.

flat.name: Mississippi
flat.note: 4% above $10,000 after the standard deduction and personal exemption.

flat.name: Pennsylvania
flat.note: 3.07% of AGI. Pennsylvania does not allow a standard deduction or personal exemption. Local earned-income tax is not included.

flat.name: Utah
flat.note: 4.5% of AGI, minus the flat taxpayer credit. The credit's income phaseout is not modeled.

ohio.name: Ohio
ohio.note: ORC 5747.02 and 5747.025 as used for 2026 (H.B. 96): $332 plus 2.75% over $26,050. Joint filing credit assumes each spouse has at least $500 of qualifying income.
